# Sampled controlled-syndrome pilot: future coverage has a real cost

28 October 2026. AUTHOR numerical study; independent audit requested. This is a floating simulation of actual ordinary calibration calls and the resulting coherent receiver, not hardware, certified theorem-budget acceptance, or execution of the rational spectral-sign/compiler algorithms.

## Physical instance and actual learner information

One fixed unknown 8-by-8 output mixer V follows independent physical bit flips on a known three-qubit repetition encoding. The physical patch is known; support localisation is not part of this pilot. The learner knows the encoder, labels it prepared, the chosen injection label, and its local Pauli settings/outcomes. V and the physical flip probability p are used only by the simulator and posthoc evaluator, not by the fitted receivers.

Native calibration prepares the normal encoded logical state. Active calibration inserts uniformly one of I,X1,X2,X3 AFTER the known encoder and BEFORE the unknown physical channel, paying two random bits and at most one extra X pulse per call. This is an additional hardware port, not a free change at a logical black box or post-source depolarization. Payload scoring uses the NORMAL uninjected native channel in every arm. The fixed logical/gauge encoding U=V U_majority is common; probe and payload error weights differ.

Every simulated call individually draws logical X/Z axis/sign, active injection if applicable, three independent physical error bits, three output Pauli axes and the actual Born outcome. Stored count tensors retain all learner-accessible sufficient statistics. No conditional-success oracle, aggregate binomial replacement for those calls, or supplied Choi matrix is used by the estimator.

The primary estimators take finite-sample signed product-Pauli shadows, fit Hermitian matrix signs, and deploy the actual three-controlled-reflection coherent SWAP into an initially maximally mixed ancilla. All physical outputs are retained until that circuit ends. Native and active-unlabelled use the same estimator. Two additional active estimators reuse exactly the SAME active records: one weights by the sum of the three known injected computational-bit labels; the other fits three individual bit reflections and then the majority sign. These are equally informed conventional refinements, not independent acquisition runs

# Independent audit: sampled controlled-syndrome calibration pilot

28 October 2026. Reviewer `producer-workspace/review_repeated_service_factorization`.

**PASS as a reproducible floating sampled-calibration pilot, not a certified acquisition theorem or hardware result.** All 512 saved banks reproduce exactly from their declared seeds using independently constructed Born probabilities. All 1,024 decoder evaluations reproduce within 4.6e-15. Author scripts, raw counts and result files were preserved; no author helper code was imported or executed by the reviewer.

## 1. What was actually simulated

The fixed source is the three-qubit repetition/syndrome subsystem followed by one dense, fixed unitary V. With representatives `e_g in {000,100,010,001}`,

`U|l,g> = V |e_g xor (111 l)>`.

The native preparation uses g=0. Active calibration first encodes the logical X± or Z± input and injects the chosen representative bit flip **before** the native independent physical bit flips and before V. Each of the three physical error bits is Bernoulli(p). Each call then selects a uniformly random product-Pauli setting and samples an actual output outcome from its eight-outcome Born distribution.

This is genuine per-call pseudorandom sampling, vectorized for computation—not a population-mean substitution or a direct draw of aggregate estimator statistics. The simulation includes random input axis, sign, active injection label when applicable, three error bits, measurement setting and measurement outcome for every call. The saved count tensor retains the learner-visible axis/sign/injection/measurement labels; it does **not** expose the sampled error pattern to the learner.

The calibration records are sampled. The subsequent performance scores are deterministic full-matrix evaluations of the learned receiver on the known simulated source, not additional sampled payload trials. V and p enter generation and posthoc scoring only. The estimator functions use the saved actual counts and known control labels.

One source V is reused throughout. The independently sampled banks are not independent draws of different sources, and the pilot does not establish behavior over an ensemble of unknown encodings.
